bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: delayed product launches (e.g., Verification delayed by 45 days); reliance on WhatsApp as primary interface; regulatory risk around fintech enablement; AI adoption by competitors; OEMs shifting marketing spend
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: highly confident, optimistic, and forward-looking — emphasized AI as core growth lever, dismissed traffic shift risks from ChatGPT, highlighted path to INR1,000cr PAT in 4-5 years
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Elite Buyer and Super Dost are not standalone apps but AI agents embedded within OLX/CarWale; monetization is shifting from seller ads to buyer fees — buyers are the largest user segment (6x sellers) and now the primary revenue engine; inspection fees (10% of remarketing revenue) are a hidden margin contributor
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet is debt-free with a ₹1,321 Cr cash reserve, and cash balance increased by roughly ₹300 Cr.
- Return on equity (year ended 31-Mar-2026) is stated at 31%, up from 10%, alongside earnings per share rising from 7 to 47 across the FY23-FY27 growth story.
- Compounding profile presented for FY23 to FY27 (Q1 FY27 annualised): revenue CAGR 22%, EBITDA CAGR 66% and PAT CAGR 54%, with PAT of ₹244 Cr described as among India's most profitable listed digital platforms.
- The deck discloses no dividend, buyback or explicit reinvestment policy - cash is simply accumulating on the balance sheet.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Unmatched infrastructure: the largest phygital auction marketplace in India with 135 Automalls, a pan-India yard and logistics network, institutional relationships with banks, NBFCs and OEMs, and ~15,000 active retail suppliers - described as the competitive moat that makes it the preferred partner for vehicle liquidation across India
- Technology-driven asset-light model: multi-platform operations on a proprietary end-to-end technology stack, highly scalable without owning inventory or building large physical assets, giving increasing operating leverage as platforms scale
- Proprietary data pool built through millions of real-world interactions and transactions, powering pricing, matching, verification and AI-led customer experiences - management calls it one of the most valuable assets it owns and one that cannot be replicated overnight
- Strong brand equity and organic reach: over 95% of traffic arrives organically; CarWale and BikeWale together attracted an average of more than 50 million unique monthly visitors with 92% organic traffic
- Synergistic network effects: as more buyers join, sellers gain a wider market and every new listing gives buyers more choice, improving price discovery, speeding matching and driving retention and loyalty
- Claimed market leadership as the #1 New Auto Marketplace, #1 Phygital Vehicle Auction Marketplace, #1 Used Goods Marketplace and #1 Used Auto Ecosystem, hosting 63% of India's used-car listings
- Experienced, founder-led leadership: Chairman and Managing Director Mr. Vinay Vinod Sanghi brings over three decades of experience in the automotive industry, with a leadership team averaging 24+ years of management experience and 14+ years of tenure at CarTrade Tech
- Financial prudence: a debt-free balance sheet and healthy cash reserves maintain stability while retaining flexibility to pursue inorganic growth opportunities with minimal impact on earnings
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Vehicle affordability pressure spilling into the used-car market — MD&A 'Threats to the Indian Automotive Outlook' states the recent surge in new vehicle prices is creating significant affordability hurdles: premium and SUV segments are thriving while entry-level cars and two-wheelers recover sluggishly, reflecting affordability pressures among middle- and lower-income households. This can spill over into the price-sensitive used-car market, driving up inventory turnover and creating pricing premiums that threaten to make even pre-owned vehicles less economically accessible - directly affecting the transaction volumes the Company monetises.
- Credit-quality deterioration in expanding used-vehicle financing portfolios — To combat affordability challenges and stimulate sales, financiers are expanding credit accessibility, including reducing initial down-payment requirements for first-time buyers in the used-car segment. The MD&A flags that aggressively expanding these lending portfolios introduces substantial credit quality risks - a structural risk to the auto-finance value chain the Company is seeking to expand into and to the demand that drives its marketplaces.
- Regulatory compliance burden on an evolving automotive regulatory framework — The MD&A identifies compliance with evolving regulatory frameworks as a threat to both manufacturing margins and market fluidity. Reduced market fluidity would compress transaction volumes across the Company's discovery, auction and remarketing platforms.
- Single-activity concentration - the entire business is one digital-marketplace activity — BRSR Section A discloses that 100.00% of turnover comes from a single main activity, 'Web search portals activities and other information service activities (Operation of web-portals, online classified media, and allied services)', NIC code 6390. The Company has no revenue diversification outside web-portal and classifieds operations, so any shock to online automotive and classifieds transaction volumes hits the whole business.
- Geographic concentration - effectively a single-country business — BRSR Section A reports zero international locations and states that international customers represented only 1.49% of total turnover in the reporting period. Revenue is therefore almost entirely exposed to Indian automotive demand, Indian regulation and Indian consumer credit conditions.
- Data protection, cybersecurity and platform-security exposure — The business depends on data from millions of user sessions to enhance customer experience, optimise inventory, position brands and calibrate search results. The Board's Directors' Report describes a robust security framework of encrypted storage, cloud infrastructure, firewalls, VPNs, multi-factor authentication, penetration testing, peer code reviews and periodic internal audits, and the Risk Management Committee's stated focus area includes cybersecurity and business continuity - identifying this as a monitored enterprise risk.
- Macro and energy-price sensitivity, and the pace of EV adoption — The MD&A outlook states the business environment faced challenges from ongoing conflicts in West Asia - shipping disruptions delayed dealer supply and delivery and hurt operating costs, while higher fuel prices affected consumer buying choices, creating a more cautious near-term demand outlook. Management explicitly states the outlook remains contingent on managing risks related to volatile energy prices and the pace of electric vehicle adoption, both of which could influence demand trends over the medium term.
- Competitive intensity from organised digital platforms and algorithmic pricing — The MD&A notes the Indian automotive market is facing increasing competition that threatens margins and market share, and that in the used-car market the deployment of algorithmic pricing engines and proprietary vehicle evaluation tools by organised digital platforms has reduced transaction latency - a competitive dynamic the Company both benefits from and must continually outspend on technology to stay ahead of.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Consumer (CarWale/BikeWale): 30% revenue growth (FY26), 96% EBITDA growth, 70-30 OEM-dealer mix; Remarketing: 22% revenue growth (FY26), 28% EBITDA margin, retail and repossession both growing; OLX India: 16% Q4 revenue growth, Verification and Elite Buyer launched, monetization nascent but accelerating; Super Dost: launched on WhatsApp, AI-driven instant matching for dealers, expanding to all OLX categories
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Claims #1 rank on three fronts simultaneously: auto portal in India, used classifieds business and vehicle auction platform, with the first two benchmarked on relative Google Trends search popularity versus key competitors (Mar-2024 to Jun-2026).
- Operates three distinct groups under one roof - Consumer Group (CarWale, BikeWale: new and used cars, two-wheelers), OLX India (online classifieds across 12 categories including auto, real estate, mobiles/electronics, furniture) and the Remarketing Group (inspection, online and phygital auctions).
- Network reach is the stated moat: ~80 Mn monthly active users across platforms (~47 Mn on CarWale/BikeWale/CarTrade and ~32 Mn on OLX India) and ~100 Mn+ cumulative app downloads.
- Remarketing serves a broad seller base - consumers, business sellers, dealers, fleet owners and OEMs - via an integrated online-offline auction platform backed by tech-enabled ERP and CRM solutions.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Partnership] The Spinny tie-up marks a shift toward partnering with, rather than only competing against, large used-car retail players, and is the template for onboarding large dealer networks.
- [Regulation] An exceptional item for 'labour law impact' of ₹307.55 lakh was booked in the quarter (₹650.71 lakh for FY26), indicating a one-off charge from new labour-law provisions.
- [Portfolio] OLX India extends the business well beyond autos into 12 classifieds categories (real estate, mobiles/electronics, furniture, etc.), diversifying the group away from a pure auto-cycle exposure.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: CarTrade Tech provides end-to-end marketplace services covering the buying, selling, marketing, valuation and financing of new and pre-owned vehicles across multiple categories, plus a horizontal used-goods classifieds platform. It serves individual buyers and sellers, dealerships, OEMs, banks, NBFCs and fleet owners through CarWale, CarTrade, BikeWale, CarWale abSure, Mobility Outlook, Shriram Automall, CarTrade Exchange, Adroit Auto and OLX India. The Company operates across three key segments - the Consumer Group, the Remarketing Group and OLX India - monetising through advertising and media solutions, lead generation and listing fees, auction commissions, SaaS solutions and value-added services.

latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: sustained double-digit growth expected across all segments; margin: expansion targeted across all businesses, OLX to reach consumer segment margins; order inflow: AI-driven buyer/seller tools to drive transaction volume; capex/commissioning: minimal — focus on tech R&D, no major capex planned
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: AI agents (matchmaking, pricing, negotiation, condition-check) for buyers/sellers; financing marketplace for used vehicle buyers (INR4,000-5,000cr transaction volume); expansion to non-auto categories (refrigerators, farm equipment); OEM trade-in partnerships for commercial vehicles
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Build 2.0, the next-generation marketplace architecture, combining proprietary marketplace intelligence, a trust framework and AI-powered agents for matching, price intelligence, condition assessment and transaction enablement
- Move from marketplaces that simply facilitate transactions to marketplaces that actively understand, anticipate and simplify them - weaving intelligence into discovery, pricing, matching and transactions
- Scale VAYA, the conversational AI interface launched in 2026, letting a customer describe what they want in their own words and a dealer list a vehicle from a single photograph
- Continue to invest in innovation, differentiated products and data-driven intelligence to build the next generation of marketplace experiences
- Retain the asset-light model - expanding reach, customers and transaction volumes without the capital intensity of owning inventory or building large physical assets, so growth translates into operating leverage
- Deploy the debt-free balance sheet and cash reserves to invest behind long-term opportunities, strengthen platforms and pursue attractive inorganic opportunities as they emerge, while remaining disciplined in capital allocation
- Expand the Company's role across the auto-financing value chain, leveraging consumer reach, the dealer ecosystem and data-driven pricing and valuation capabilities
- Grow OLX India as a broad, horizontal marketplace for used products in a market that remains far more fragmented and less organised than the new-products market
- Deepen partnerships across the ecosystem - OEMs reaching high-intent buyers, dealers using DMS/CRM, inspection, valuation and certified retail, and banking partners bringing financing closer to the point of decision
- Sharpen consumer tools across the vehicle-buying journey - discovery, comparison, valuation, financing and transaction - as that journey moves increasingly online
- Prioritise hiring in technology, operations, sales and marketing, using a structured Employee Stock Option Plan to encourage an entrepreneurial mindset and retain talent
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: CarTrade Tech runs a fully asset-light platform model: it enables and executes transactions while partners hold the underlying inventory and provide financing and logistics, keeping the model capital-efficient and scalable without balance-sheet intensity, and its scalable technology framework is described as enabling efficient growth with minimal capital needs. Expansion is therefore footprint and platform build-out rather than plant capex. The physical footprint spans over 500 locations across 135 cities, combining CarWale abSure, OLX and Shriram Automall, with 135 Automalls forming the largest phygital auction marketplace in India, supported by a pan-India yard and logistics network. Platform build-out in FY26 centred on technology: the Company introduced CarTrade Labs in 2025 as a dedicated innovation hub driving AI, data science and digital transformation across the ecosystem, and launched VAYA AI in 2026, a conversational interface letting customers describe what they want in their own words and dealers list a vehicle from a single photograph. Management is now building 2.0, the next-generation marketplace architecture combining proprietary marketplace intelligence, a trust framework and AI-powered agents for matching, price intelligence, condition assessment and transaction enablement, and is integrating agentic AI into matchmaking. Earlier expansion came through acquisition rather than construction - CarWale and BikeWale in 2016, a stake in Shriram Automall in 2018 and OLX India in 2023. The BRSR reports no plants and four national offices; a studio in Panvel, Maharashtra was closed during FY 2025-26. The registered and corporate office moves from Vishwaroop IT Park, Vashi to Shree Sawan Knowledge Park, Turbhe, Navi Mumbai with effect from June 01, 2026. The Company also migrated its accounting system to Oracle NetSuite from Navision in October 2025. Management states it has the financial strength and flexibility, with zero debt, to invest behind long-term opportunities, strengthen platforms and pursue attractive inorganic opportunities as they emerge.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Auto sales witnessed unprecedented levels during the year driven by the strong sentiment created by GST rationalisation and multiple repo rate revisions by the RBI
- India's used-car market is projected to expand at a 14-18% CAGR over the next five years to ~$70 billion, becoming the third-largest used-car market in the world
- Used-car financing penetration is anticipated to reach between 30% and 40% by FY27, up from 20-30% in FY22, as NBFC used-car loan approvals scale rapidly
- Replacement cycles are projected to decline from 7-8 years in FY21 to 4-5 years by FY31, and the used-to-new car ratio in India is 1.4x versus 2-3x in mature global markets - large headroom for growth
- The total addressable market for used cars is projected to reach 280 million households by FY2030-31, with only 1 in 10 households currently owning a car and household incomes growing
- The Indian two-wheeler used market is projected to expand from ~21.3 million two-wheelers to ~55.8 million units by 2027, aided by affordability, digital innovation and rising trust in organised platforms
- The automotive testing, inspection and certification market was valued at $20.31 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow at a 4.78% CAGR to $26.86 billion by 2031
- The global used-commercial-vehicle market is projected to scale from ~$47.2 billion in 2025 to $79.8 billion by 2032, at an 8.1% CAGR over 2026-2032
- India's digital advertising market is projected to grow at a ~15% CAGR between 2024 and 2029; India spent ~$11 billion on digital advertising in 2025, projected to grow at a 10-15% CAGR over the next five years
- India's digital classifieds market contributes only ~4% of total retail used-car sales by volume in FY2025-26, leaving significant headroom for organised digital platforms
- Consumer and business preference is shifting towards organised players for selling pre-owned vehicles through auctions, which the integrated online and offline presence is positioned to capture
- Artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing what customers expect from a digital marketplace - experiences are becoming more intuitive, personalised and responsive
- India's economic outlook remains cautiously positive with FY26 GDP growth of 7.7% and planned central-government capital expenditure growth of 11.5% in FY2026-27
- Near-term demand outlook is more cautious - West Asia conflicts caused shipping delays that hurt dealer operating costs and higher fuel prices that affected consumer buying choices
- The outlook remains contingent on managing risks related to volatile energy prices and the pace of electric vehicle adoption, both of which could influence demand trends over the medium term
- Rising vehicle prices are creating affordability hurdles: premium and SUV segments are thriving while entry-level cars and two-wheelers recover sluggishly, which can spill over into the price-sensitive used-car market
- Revenue growth was described as broad-based, with the consumer group the leading contributor, and margin expansion driven by higher operating leverage, revenue growth across key business segments and disciplined cost management
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: CarTrade Tech delivered strong Q4FY26 growth with 54% PAT growth and 35% EBITDA margin, driven by AI-powered monetization initiatives like Elite Buyer and Super Dost that are accelerating buyer-side revenue streams; the shift from pure advertising to transaction-based monetization and margin expansion across all segments positions the company for sustained profitability and a path to INR1,000cr PAT in 4-5 years.

open.item: New OLX products enabling consumers and dealers to buy/sell used products are under development and will start rolling out over the next few quarters, with management expecting increased monetization from them.
open.promised: new revenue streams rolled out text

open.item: Management expects remarketing growth and absolute numbers to get better in Q4, which is seasonally much stronger than Q3, tracking the 22% 9-month revenue growth rate.
OLX will launch a new Verification product to enhance trust and safety on the platform within the next 30 days.
Management said it sees no reason for the consumer group's 32% 9-month revenue growth rate to come down and expects it to sustain.
Management guided that OLX's revenue growth rate will go up from the current 18% year-on-year in the January-March quarter.
Management said the dip in auction conversion caused by the GST-driven used-vehicle price reset is temporary and conversion will pick up in coming quarters, and is already better.
Management cited the consensus view that the Indian automotive (car) industry will grow 0-5% in FY26, similar to last year, and expects no change in market dynamics.
Management says OLX's 12% YoY quarterly revenue growth (16% for the full year) will improve in coming quarters and years as product initiatives play out.
Consumer group marketing spend was Rs 7.6 crores in Q4 (just over 10% of that segment's revenue) and management expects no material variation in marketing cost going forward.
open.promised: Rs 7.6 cr per quarter, stable INR cr

open.item: Management explicitly declined to give FY26 revenue/growth guidance for the consumer business, saying not much has changed in the industry.
Repossessed vehicles are now about 54% of the remarketing inventory sold and management expects repossession volumes to keep growing over the next few quarters, benefiting SAMIL/Shriram Automall.
Consumer group revenue mix stayed at roughly 65% OEM and 35% dealer in FY25, and management does not see a reason for that trend to change next year.

The single biggest internal effort for the year is further investment in product and technology, including AI tools, across the whole group (CarWale, BikeWale, OLX, Automall), expensed within operating cost.
open.promised: group-wide product/tech and AI build-out text

open.item: Standalone ESOP cost of Rs 2.79 crore per quarter (Rs 8.36 crore for nine months, down 37% YoY) is expected to keep declining next year as older grants vest out.
The registered and corporate office relocates from Vishwaroop IT Park, Vashi, Navi Mumbai to Shree Sawan Knowledge Park, TTC MIDC Industrial Area, Turbhe, Navi Mumbai with effect from June 01, 2026.

Management said OLX revenue growth will step up from the current ~16% year-on-year rate, with monetization momentum becoming visible from Q1FY27 or Q2FY27, though it declined to give a numeric guidance.
Company will launch used-car financing products with large banks and NBFCs on a pure marketplace model, taking no balance sheet or lending risk, in the next few quarters.
Management guided that EBITDA margins will expand across all three businesses in FY27, including the consumer business (38% in FY26) and OLX (31% in FY26).

Management guided that costs are likely to remain quite stable in FY27, and specifically that OLX employee cost will not change much next year (FY26 employee cost up only 4%, from Rs 73 crores to Rs 75 crores, with total OLX cost growth of 1%).

The company will build and roll out a series of proprietary AI agents during FY27 - matchmaking, pricing, negotiation and condition-check agents now, followed by listing, buying and loan agents - across OLX and CarWale.

verdicts.item: Repossession is back to about 50% of remarketing auction volume (from ~42%) and management expects these volumes to sustain or grow from here.

verdicts.item: Consumer-group performance depends on auto supply exceeding demand; management expects that favourable condition to persist for the next few quarters with no real change in industry growth rates.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 2Q past horizon Q2FY26

verdicts.item: CarWale and OLX will keep separate consumer/dealer front-ends but merge backend systems, with the first common backend functions going live in the current quarter.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Finance offers for new cars, two-wheelers and used cars are live on CarWale, BikeWale and now OLX, with two-wheeler volumes scaling, but management said these will not be meaningful monetisation in the next 3-6 months.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 3Q past horizon Q1FY26

wtt.tone_latest: Highly confident and repeatedly optimistic on FY27 monetization and margins, refusing year-by-year guidance in favour of a 4-5 year Rs 1,000 crores PAT goal; management did own two misses - the ~45-day delay in launching Verification behind the softer OLX growth, and the 10% ROE being below cost of capital due to the idle cash pile.

The physical footprint spans over 500 locations across 135 cities, combining CarWale abSure, OLX and Shriram Automall, with 135 Automalls forming the largest phygital auction marketplace in India, supported by a pan-India yard and logistics network. Platform build-out in FY26 centred on technology: the Company introduced CarTrade Labs in 2025 as a dedicated innovation hub driving AI, data science and digital transformation across the ecosystem, and launched VAYA AI in 2026, a conversational interface letting customers describe what they want in their own words and dealers list a vehicle from a single photograph. The registered and corporate office moves from Vishwaroop IT Park, Vashi to Shree Sawan Knowledge Park, Turbhe, Navi Mumbai with effect from June 01, 2026. The Company also migrated its accounting system to Oracle NetSuite from Navision in October 2025. Management states it has the financial strength and flexibility, with zero debt, to invest behind long-term opportunities, strengthen platforms and pursue attractive inorganic opportunities as they emerge.

risks.risk: Vehicle affordability pressure spilling into the used-car market
risks.note: MD&A 'Threats to the Indian Automotive Outlook' states the recent surge in new vehicle prices is creating significant affordability hurdles: premium and SUV segments are thriving while entry-level cars and two-wheelers recover sluggishly, reflecting affordability pressures among middle- and lower-income households. This can spill over into the price-sensitive used-car market, driving up inventory turnover and creating pricing premiums that threaten to make even pre-owned vehicles less economically accessible - directly affecting the transaction volumes the Company monetises.

risks.risk: Credit-quality deterioration in expanding used-vehicle financing portfolios
risks.note: To combat affordability challenges and stimulate sales, financiers are expanding credit accessibility, including reducing initial down-payment requirements for first-time buyers in the used-car segment. The MD&A flags that aggressively expanding these lending portfolios introduces substantial credit quality risks - a structural risk to the auto-finance value chain the Company is seeking to expand into and to the demand that drives its marketplaces.

risks.risk: Regulatory compliance burden on an evolving automotive regulatory framework
risks.note: The MD&A identifies compliance with evolving regulatory frameworks as a threat to both manufacturing margins and market fluidity. Reduced market fluidity would compress transaction volumes across the Company's discovery, auction and remarketing platforms.

risks.risk: Single-activity concentration - the entire business is one digital-marketplace activity
risks.note: BRSR Section A discloses that 100.00% of turnover comes from a single main activity, 'Web search portals activities and other information service activities (Operation of web-portals, online classified media, and allied services)', NIC code 6390. The Company has no revenue diversification outside web-portal and classifieds operations, so any shock to online automotive and classifieds transaction volumes hits the whole business.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration - effectively a single-country business
risks.note: BRSR Section A reports zero international locations and states that international customers represented only 1.49% of total turnover in the reporting period. Revenue is therefore almost entirely exposed to Indian automotive demand, Indian regulation and Indian consumer credit conditions.

risks.risk: Data protection, cybersecurity and platform-security exposure
risks.note: The business depends on data from millions of user sessions to enhance customer experience, optimise inventory, position brands and calibrate search results. The Board's Directors' Report describes a robust security framework of encrypted storage, cloud infrastructure, firewalls, VPNs, multi-factor authentication, penetration testing, peer code reviews and periodic internal audits, and the Risk Management Committee's stated focus area includes cybersecurity and business continuity - identifying this as a monitored enterprise risk.

risks.risk: Macro and energy-price sensitivity, and the pace of EV adoption
risks.note: The MD&A outlook states the business environment faced challenges from ongoing conflicts in West Asia - shipping disruptions delayed dealer supply and delivery and hurt operating costs, while higher fuel prices affected consumer buying choices, creating a more cautious near-term demand outlook. Management explicitly states the outlook remains contingent on managing risks related to volatile energy prices and the pace of electric vehicle adoption, both of which could influence demand trends over the medium term.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity from organised digital platforms and algorithmic pricing
risks.note: The MD&A notes the Indian automotive market is facing increasing competition that threatens margins and market share, and that in the used-car market the deployment of algorithmic pricing engines and proprietary vehicle evaluation tools by organised digital platforms has reduced transaction latency - a competitive dynamic the Company both benefits from and must continually outspend on technology to stay ahead of.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: CarTrade Tech provides end-to-end marketplace services covering the buying, selling, marketing, valuation and financing of new and pre-owned vehicles across multiple categories, plus a horizontal used-goods classifieds platform. It serves individual buyers and sellers, dealerships, OEMs, banks, NBFCs and fleet owners through CarWale, CarTrade, BikeWale, CarWale abSure, Mobility Outlook, Shriram Automall, CarTrade Exchange, Adroit Auto and OLX India. The Company operates across three key segments - the Consumer Group, the Remarketing Group and OLX India - monetising through advertising and media solutions, lead generation and listing fees, auction commissions, SaaS solutions and value-added services.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Auto sales witnessed unprecedented levels during the year driven by the strong sentiment created by GST rationalisation and multiple repo rate revisions by the RBI
- India's used-car market is projected to expand at a 14-18% CAGR over the next five years to ~$70 billion, becoming the third-largest used-car market in the world
- Used-car financing penetration is anticipated to reach between 30% and 40% by FY27, up from 20-30% in FY22, as NBFC used-car loan approvals scale rapidly
- Replacement cycles are projected to decline from 7-8 years in FY21 to 4-5 years by FY31, and the used-to-new car ratio in India is 1.4x versus 2-3x in mature global markets - large headroom for growth
- The total addressable market for used cars is projected to reach 280 million households by FY2030-31, with only 1 in 10 households currently owning a car and household incomes growing
- The Indian two-wheeler used market is projected to expand from ~21.3 million two-wheelers to ~55.8 million units by 2027, aided by affordability, digital innovation and rising trust in organised platforms
- The automotive testing, inspection and certification market was valued at $20.31 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow at a 4.78% CAGR to $26.86 billion by 2031
- The global used-commercial-vehicle market is projected to scale from ~$47.2 billion in 2025 to $79.8 billion by 2032, at an 8.1% CAGR over 2026-2032
- India's digital advertising market is projected to grow at a ~15% CAGR between 2024 and 2029; India spent ~$11 billion on digital advertising in 2025, projected to grow at a 10-15% CAGR over the next five years
- India's digital classifieds market contributes only ~4% of total retail used-car sales by volume in FY2025-26, leaving significant headroom for organised digital platforms
- Consumer and business preference is shifting towards organised players for selling pre-owned vehicles through auctions, which the integrated online and offline presence is positioned to capture
- Artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing what customers expect from a digital marketplace - experiences are becoming more intuitive, personalised and responsive
- India's economic outlook remains cautiously positive with FY26 GDP growth of 7.7% and planned central-government capital expenditure growth of 11.5% in FY2026-27
- Near-term demand outlook is more cautious - West Asia conflicts caused shipping delays that hurt dealer operating costs and higher fuel prices that affected consumer buying choices
- The outlook remains contingent on managing risks related to volatile energy prices and the pace of electric vehicle adoption, both of which could influence demand trends over the medium term
- Rising vehicle prices are creating affordability hurdles: premium and SUV segments are thriving while entry-level cars and two-wheelers recover sluggishly, which can spill over into the price-sensitive used-car market
- Revenue growth was described as broad-based, with the consumer group the leading contributor, and margin expansion driven by higher operating leverage, revenue growth across key business segments and disciplined cost management

capex_expansion.body: CarTrade Tech runs a fully asset-light platform model: it enables and executes transactions while partners hold the underlying inventory and provide financing and logistics, keeping the model capital-efficient and scalable without balance-sheet intensity, and its scalable technology framework is described as enabling efficient growth with minimal capital needs. Expansion is therefore footprint and platform build-out rather than plant capex. The physical footprint spans over 500 locations across 135 cities, combining CarWale abSure, OLX and Shriram Automall, with 135 Automalls forming the largest phygital auction marketplace in India, supported by a pan-India yard and logistics network. Platform build-out in FY26 centred on technology: the Company introduced CarTrade Labs in 2025 as a dedicated innovation hub driving AI, data science and digital transformation across the ecosystem, and launched VAYA AI in 2026, a conversational interface letting customers describe what they want in their own words and dealers list a vehicle from a single photograph. Management is now building 2.0, the next-generation marketplace architecture combining proprietary marketplace intelligence, a trust framework and AI-powered agents for matching, price intelligence, condition assessment and transaction enablement, and is integrating agentic AI into matchmaking. Earlier expansion came through acquisition rather than construction - CarWale and BikeWale in 2016, a stake in Shriram Automall in 2018 and OLX India in 2023. The BRSR reports no plants and four national offices; a studio in Panvel, Maharashtra was closed during FY 2025-26. The registered and corporate office moves from Vishwaroop IT Park, Vashi to Shree Sawan Knowledge Park, Turbhe, Navi Mumbai with effect from June 01, 2026. The Company also migrated its accounting system to Oracle NetSuite from Navision in October 2025. Management states it has the financial strength and flexibility, with zero debt, to invest behind long-term opportunities, strengthen platforms and pursue attractive inorganic opportunities as they emerge.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: highly confident, optimistic, and forward-looking — emphasized AI as core growth lever, dismissed traffic shift risks from ChatGPT, highlighted path to INR1,000cr PAT in 4-5 years

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Unmatched infrastructure: the largest phygital auction marketplace in India with 135 Automalls, a pan-India yard and logistics network, institutional relationships with banks, NBFCs and OEMs, and ~15,000 active retail suppliers - described as the competitive moat that makes it the preferred partner for vehicle liquidation across India
- Technology-driven asset-light model: multi-platform operations on a proprietary end-to-end technology stack, highly scalable without owning inventory or building large physical assets, giving increasing operating leverage as platforms scale
- Proprietary data pool built through millions of real-world interactions and transactions, powering pricing, matching, verification and AI-led customer experiences - management calls it one of the most valuable assets it owns and one that cannot be replicated overnight
- Strong brand equity and organic reach: over 95% of traffic arrives organically; CarWale and BikeWale together attracted an average of more than 50 million unique monthly visitors with 92% organic traffic
- Synergistic network effects: as more buyers join, sellers gain a wider market and every new listing gives buyers more choice, improving price discovery, speeding matching and driving retention and loyalty
- Claimed market leadership as the #1 New Auto Marketplace, #1 Phygital Vehicle Auction Marketplace, #1 Used Goods Marketplace and #1 Used Auto Ecosystem, hosting 63% of India's used-car listings
- Experienced, founder-led leadership: Chairman and Managing Director Mr. Vinay Vinod Sanghi brings over three decades of experience in the automotive industry, with a leadership team averaging 24+ years of management experience and 14+ years of tenure at CarTrade Tech
- Financial prudence: a debt-free balance sheet and healthy cash reserves maintain stability while retaining flexibility to pursue inorganic growth opportunities with minimal impact on earnings

non_obvious.body: Elite Buyer and Super Dost are not standalone apps but AI agents embedded within OLX/CarWale; monetization is shifting from seller ads to buyer fees — buyers are the largest user segment (6x sellers) and now the primary revenue engine; inspection fees (10% of remarketing revenue) are a hidden margin contributor

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Partnership] The Spinny tie-up marks a shift toward partnering with, rather than only competing against, large used-car retail players, and is the template for onboarding large dealer networks.
- [Regulation] An exceptional item for 'labour law impact' of ₹307.55 lakh was booked in the quarter (₹650.71 lakh for FY26), indicating a one-off charge from new labour-law provisions.
- [Portfolio] OLX India extends the business well beyond autos into 12 classifieds categories (real estate, mobiles/electronics, furniture, etc.), diversifying the group away from a pure auto-cycle exposure.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV.
